title: PRD: Endpoint Acceptance Playbook for Composable Hosted Lanes (chat / embeddings / rerank) - slice-driven launch & graded fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a concise PRD and operational launch playbook for composable hosted lanes covering chat, completion-style generation, embeddings, and rerank endpoints. This ticket captures acceptance criteria, slice-driven rollout strategy, telemetry gates, fallback model variants, and the launch checklist required for a progressive, low-risk cutover.
goals: Ship a single operable bundle of hosted lanes (chat, completion, embedding, rerank) with unified telemetry, deterministic acceptance gates, and graded fallbacks.
Enable slice-based canary traffic that isolates behavioral regressions to small cohorts (0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%).
Ensure SLOs: p95 latency targets per lane, error rate <0.5% on steady load, and quality regressions below defined eval thresholds.
Provide a clear operator checklist for cutover, rollback, and post-launch monitoring responsibilities.
non_goals: Major SDK changes or protocol redesigns (this PRD assumes current API surface remains stable).
Onboarding new model families that require runtime kernel rewrites (those get separate model-onboarding PRDs).
Replacing dedicated/private deployment flows — this is focused on Hosted API.
assumptions: Model variants with compatible behavior exist (base, quantized, and fallbacks).
Runtime supports graded routing and per-tenant traffic slices via existing router policies.
Telemetry (per-token cost, token latency, quality signals) is available in Console dashboards and can be sliced by traffic cohort.
requirements: API contracts: endpoints must accept the existing unified interaction payloads and return stable schema (content, metadata, model_id, cost_breakdown).
Behavioural contracts: deterministic output profile for golden prompts used in eval slices (per-lane eval sets).
Operational contracts: automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model on latency SLO breach or capacity shortage.
Security/compliance: request/response audit logging enabled for canary tenants; KMS-backed encryption for any persisted artifacts.
api_contract: /v1/hosted/chat -> supports streaming + function-calling + tool attachments, maintains message ids for deduping.
/v1/hosted/completions -> supports max_tokens, temperature bands and deterministic seed for eval slices.
/v1/hosted/embeddings -> deterministic vector signatures for same input and model_id; stable dimension output.
/v1/hosted/rerank -> accepts scored candidate sets, returns stable ranking with confidence scores and explainability hints.
All endpoints return a model_variant field and exposure tags for fallback decisions.
rollout_strategy: Stage 0: Internal shadow traffic + synthetic load for 3 days (no user-facing traffic).
Stage 1: 0.5% real traffic (lighthouse tenants) for 24-48 hours; run eval slices and monitor quality regressions.
Stage 2: 5% traffic for 48-72 hours with automatic metric gates; if gates pass, progress to Stage 3.
Stage 3: 25% traffic for 72 hours; stress test autoscale and latency SLOs with targeted load ramps.
Stage 4: 100% traffic cutover with monitoring and extended post-launch support window (72 hours).
At every stage: policy enforces graded fallbacks by model_variant compatibility and region-aware routing.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: All four endpoints respond with correct schema and pass conformance tests in the staging harness.
Behavioral: Eval slice quality delta from incumbent <= 2% for embeddings similarity, <= 3% for chat reproduction tests, and rerank NDCG drop <= 1.5%.
Reliability: p95 latency <= lane target (chat: 300ms, completion: 220ms, embeddings: 150ms, rerank: 250ms) under accepted traffic profile.
Error budget: Error rate (5xx + 4xx errors attributable to runtime) < 0.5% during canary stages.
Cost: Per-token unit cost against baseline within +/-10% for initial rollout; deviations must be approved by FinOps.
Safety: No high-severity safety incidents in eval slices; any flagged safety issues must be remediated before progressing beyond Stage 1.
Observability: Console shows token-level cost, model-level latency, per-slice quality metrics, and alerting hooks wired to on-call.
launch_checklist: Engineering: Merge prod-ready PRs and tag runtime release (release: hosted-api-2026.03).
QA: Run automated conformance suite + manual exploratory on the golden prompt set for each lane.
Evals: Publish eval slice report with aggregated metrics and signal quality deltas vs baseline.
SRE/Ops: Configure traffic slices, canary routing policies, and graded fallback policies; verify autoscaler playbooks.
Security: Confirm audit logging and KMS integration for canary tenants; run quick SSO smoke test for RBAC tenants.
Console: Create lane dashboards (latency, errors, cost) and open-ended trace links for quick triage.
Runbook: Publish cutover runbook and rollback steps, assign post-launch pager and 72-hour war room schedule.
Comms: Notify internal stakeholders and customer success for known early adopters; publish status page template.
risks: Quality regressions that only appear at larger cohorts (mitigated by staged slices and quick rollback).
Autoscaler misconfiguration leading to transient latency spikes (mitigated by load ramps and stress tests).
Fallback incompatibility causing semantic drift for a subset of tenants (mitigated by compatibility matrix and regression tests).
Operational overhead during staged launch requiring dedicated SRE/PM on-call for 72 hours.
dependencies: ENG-21402: Router policy improvements for per-slice weighting and deterministic hashing.
ENG-22098: Telemetry pipeline extension for per-slice eval metrics and cost breakdowns.
ENG-22600: Fallback model-variant contract and automated swap tooling.
